notes.summary: Conditional constant meromorphic field and exclusion of all separated finite-type algebraic-space algebraizations; finite wide-polyannulus Picard vanishing remains unproved.
notes.detailedSummary: For K=C((s)), |s|=exp(-1/8), t=s^8 and periods (t,2),(3,t), the ordinary quotient geometry is established. Assuming Pic(P_m,L)=0 for every finite wide polyannulus over a given complete extension L, inner Gauss bounds give compatible infinite frames, and the signed theta recurrence and common pole fractions prove Γ(X_L,M)=L. Smooth finite-type algebraic-space descent, generic-field hypotheses and analytic flatness then rule out every separated finite-type algebraization. Gruson IV.5 has insufficient scope to discharge the explicit Picard condition.
notes.text:
Fix K=C((s)), |s|=exp(-1/8), t=s^8, v=-log|.|. Put T=(G_m²)^an, λ1=(t,2), λ2=(3,t), Λ=〈λ1,λ2〉 and x=(-log|z1|,-log|z2|). The geometric construction below is unconditional in the standard Berkovich foundational setting. The subsequent nonalgebraization conclusion is explicitly conditional on F_L, which is not established here.

The quotient X=T/Λ exists and is good, strict, smooth, separated, boundaryless, proper, geometrically connected and purely two-dimensional. Indeed x(λ(n)z)=x(z)+n. For an open rectangle B of widths less than one, x^-1(B) has disjoint deck translates and gives an ordinary open quotient chart. On overlaps the deck element is locally constant; multiplication by λ(n) gives analytic transitions satisfying the cocycle. For compact C,D only finitely many n can lie in x(D)-x(C), hence can make λ(n)C meet D. Relatively compact neighborhoods and separation of their finitely many relevant translates separate distinct orbits. For analytic separatedness, the inverse image of the diagonal is the locally finite disjoint union of closed translation graphs in T×_K T. Closed-immersion descent on the sheet atlas gives the closed diagonal. The strict compact polyannulus x^-1([0,1]²) surjects, so X is compact. For any point choose a center in (1/8 Z)² within 1/16 in each coordinate, an outer chart rectangle of width 3/4 and an inner closed rectangle of width 1/2. The inner inverse image is a strict affinoid neighborhood. This proves goodness and strictness. Ordinary-open torus charts prove smoothness, pure dimension two and empty relative boundary. Compactness, separatedness and empty boundary imply properness. The same charts and periods construct X_L over every complete isometric extension L/K. Increasing integral Laurent polyannuli exhaust T_L, so T_L and its quotient are connected. Regular components are locally finite and disjoint, giving integrality from connectedness. None of these arguments uses F_L.

There are τ:X→R²/Z² and a closed Gauss section i. At x the Laurent-polynomial seminorm is max_m |a_m|exp(-m·x). The graded Laurent domain proves multiplicativity, and evaluations prove continuity. Translation takes the Gauss point at x to that at x+n. Thus τ and i descend, τi=id, and i has closed image because its domain is compact and X is Hausdorff.

The missing foundation F_L is precisely: Pic(P_m,L)=0 for every integer m≥1, where P_m,L={|s|^m≤|z_j|≤|s|^-m, j=1,2}. No conclusion for an extension L is asserted without F_L for that extension. Van der Put, Rigid analytic spaces (1975–76), 3.4.8, prints the broader sufficient assertion that regular factorial affinoid B remains factorial after adjoining a restricted disc or unit-circle variable. His 3.4.9 extends a line bundle across an inner disc and applies this assertion; in the second-coordinate step its base is already a wide annulus. Gruson, Fibrés vectoriels sur un polydisque ultramétrique (1968), IV.5 Theorem 1, instead treats completed tensor products of discs T_(1,r), r in the divisible hull of the value group, and unit circles C. Its immediate proof uses a polynomial/Laurent polynomial graded algebra over gr(K). It does not establish arbitrary wide-annulus-base factoriality. A nonzero-width annulus is not a unit circle. Neither that narrower theorem nor Papikian's deferred-proof discussion discharges F_L.

Here is the complete remaining implication. Write a=-log|s|. For a unit f=Σ b_βz^β on P_m, its Gauss log norm N_f(y)=max_β(log|b_β|+β·y), y∈[-ma,ma]², and the norm of its inverse are convex and sum to zero. Hence N_f is affine. A Laurent term attaining the norm at an interior point supplies its integral slope α. Vertex inequalities give |b_β/b_α|exp(ma|β-α|_1)≤1. Therefore f=bz^α(1+g), with zero constant coefficient in g and ||g||_(P_j)≤|s|^(m-j) whenever j<m. Smallness on P_m's boundary is not claimed. On all R² the same argument forces every global torus unit to be exactly bz^α, since any different exponent would exceed the affine norm on a ray.

Assume F_L and choose frames e_m of a line bundle on P_m. Normalize each new frame by a scalar monomial so that e_(m+1)|P_m=(1+g_m)e_m with the preceding bounds. For fixed j, ∏_(m=j)^∞(1+g_m)|P_j converges to a unit: its first term is already a unit, and later errors have norm tending to zero, eventually less than one; inverse products also converge. The frames E_j=e_j∏_(m=j)^∞(1+g_m)|P_j satisfy E_(j+1)|P_j=E_j. They glue along the exhaustion, proving Pic(T_L)=0. Independent finite trivializations alone would not prove this.

Pull a line bundle on X_L to T_L and choose its global frame. A section satisfies θ(λz)=c_λz^(h_λ)θ(z). Its multipliers are torus units, hence monomials. Commuting deck actions give additive h and λ^(h_λ′)=(λ′)^(h_λ). If h_λ1=(A,B), h_λ2=(C,D), then t^C2^D=3^At^B. Valuation gives C=B; unique prime factorization in Q gives A=D=0. Thus h_λ1=(0,k), h_λ2=(k,0). If k≠0 choose n=(1,sign k), λ=λ(n) and h=(kn2,kn1). Then Q=v(λ^h)=2|k|>0. For a nonzero Laurent coefficient a_m, comparison gives a_(m+jh)=a_m c_λ^j λ^(-jm-hj(j+1)/2). Its valuation tends to -∞, contradicting Laurent coefficient decay on the fixed unit polyannulus. If k=0, every nonzero coefficient obeys λ_i^m=c_i. Two such exponents have λ_i^(m-m′)=1; their valuations force m=m′. The section is one scalar monomial, has no zeros and trivializes its descended bundle. In particular X_L has no nonzero effective analytic Cartier divisor.

For an arbitrary nonzero meromorphic F on X_L, its pullback to the smooth torus has an effective Cartier pole divisor P. Regular local rings make the local pole ideals invertible, and they glue. Pic(T_L)=0 trivializes O(-P); its inclusion into O gives a global analytic θ0 with divisor P. Then θ1=Fθ0 has no height-one poles, so normality, by intersection of height-one valuation rings on each normal affinoid, makes it analytic. The pair has no common height-one divisor. Deck invariance of P makes θ0(λz)/θ0(z) a meromorphic unit with zero divisor; normality of it and its inverse makes it an analytic torus unit. Both θi have the same multiplier. The recurrence therefore forces them to be scalar multiples of the same monomial. Consequently Γ(X_L,M)=L. This treats all meromorphic fractions, not selected characters.

Suppose a separated finite-type L-algebraic space Y has Y^an≅X_L. Conrad–Temkin, Non-archimedean analytification of algebraic spaces, Theorem 2.3.1, preserves and reflects smoothness; Example 2.3.2 identifies closed-point residue fields and completed local rings. The complete applied statements and immediate proofs were freshly read. Applying the associated rigid-space formulation, Y is smooth of dimension two. A nontrivial clopen decomposition would analytify to one; each nonempty finite-type piece has a closed point and nonempty analytification. Thus Y is connected. Its finitely many regular irreducible components are disjoint and open, so it is integral.

All Stacks 0ENA hypotheses hold: regular noetherian charts have only codimension-zero weakly associated points; finite-type noetherian étale charts satisfy 0BB1's finite-component conditions; separatedness implies decency and generic field monomorphisms. By 086U the schematic locus is dense and contains the generic point. Tags 0ENA and 0END identify global algebraic meromorphic functions with the generic field. A dense affine schematic open and Noether normalization give trdeg_L L(Y)=2.

Analytic passage needs an additional input. Ducros, Families of Berkovich spaces, 2.1.4, states that algebraic-to-analytic local-ring maps are regular, hence flat, citing Berkovich (1993), 2.6.2, and Ducros (2009), 3.3. These are honestly cited deeper published foundations. A local flat map is faithfully flat and preserves nonzerodivisors. For reduced noetherian affinoid A and finite faithfully flat étale B, localization gives products of fields, so Q(B)=Q(A)⊗_A B and faithful-flat descent gives the equalizer Q(A)→Q(B)⇉Q(B⊗_A B). This calculation alone is not a general analytic meromorphic-descent theorem. In the present case, the algebraic Cartier pole divisor, its invertible sheaf and its two regular sections descend algebraically and analytify by Conrad–Temkin §2.3. Nonzerodivisor preservation on scheme charts descends through faithfully flat analytic étale charts, making their ratio a global analytic meromorphic function. For injectivity, choose a closed point outside V(gh) for a nonzero fraction g/h on a dense affine schematic open. Its finite residue extension is complete, and the corresponding analytic point has nonzero value. Thus L(Y) injects into Γ(X_L,M)=L while fixing L, contradicting transcendence degree two.

This conditional theorem excludes all separated finite-type schemes and algebraic spaces, without projectivity or a GAGA group-law premise. F_L remains unresolved, so no unconditional nonalgebraization certificate is issued. The unconditional selected integral-period matrices are [[0,k],[k,0]], none positive definite; that period obstruction alone is insufficient. Complete artifacts are nonalgebraization-conditional-paper.md, P16.7-partial-paper.md, proof-companion.md and source-application-ledger.md. Own finite checks rerun with `python scripts/diagnostics.py`; they do not prove the universal analytic assertions.

notes.summary: Repaired middle-positive bounded CLD operator, raw mass 2, bounded comparison and actual off-canonical-skeleton mass-one atoms; no unbounded E¹ extension.
notes.detailedSummary: On the unconditional quotient geometry of n1, θ=d′d″((x₁²+x₂²)/2) defines a real analytic positivity datum. Middle PSD domination and coefficient measures, with a concrete Plücker obstruction to the strong-cone shortcut, construct ordinary-local symmetric positive mixed measures on the continuous locally smooth-positive approximant class C_θ. The operator has mass 2 and uniform continuity and bounded comparison. Explicit U_N contain a genuine analytic atom δ_(ξ_N) of mass one off the original Gauss section. No recognition of a full psh class, decreasing unbounded continuity or full uniqueness is claimed.
notes.text:
This note uses only n1's unconditional quotient geometry, not F_L. It constructs a bounded locally generated ordinary CLD theory and an actual off-canonical-skeleton atom. It does not identify its class with classical curve-test psh, semipositive model PL, weak-smooth psh or a full intrinsic psh cone.

On a deck sheet put x_j=-log|z_j| and q=(x_1²+x_2²)/2. Since q(x+n)-q(x)=n·x+|n|²/2 has d′d″=0, θ=d′d″q descends. Define C_θ to be the continuous real functions u on X such that q+u is locally, on ordinary opens, a locally uniform limit of ordinary CLD smooth functions with middle-positive Hessian. This specified generated class is not defined circularly through the operator constructed below. Its functions are bounded because X is compact.

The ambient cone repair is essential. A symmetric (p,p) coefficient form is a symmetric matrix on Λ^p V, with the usual sign convention. Middle positivity is positive semidefiniteness. Strong positivity is generated by ww^t with w decomposable. For dim V=4, p=2, every w=a∧b satisfies w12w34-w13w24+w14w23=0. The resulting linear functional on symmetric coefficient matrices vanishes on the span of strong squares, but takes value one on (e12+e34)(e12+e34)^t. Thus strong squares do not span all ambient symmetric forms. Analytic dimension two does not establish the contrary assertion for arbitrary-dimensional moment presentations.

For middle positivity a Euclidean positive form λ has λ^p represented by p! times a positive definite identity matrix. On a fixed compact tropical support, every smooth symmetric coefficient matrix B satisfies -Cλ^p≤B≤Cλ^p for some finite C. A smooth nonnegative cutoff equal to one on that support and compactly supported in the SAME ordinary open gives a decomposition into two compactly supported middle-positive forms. A finite moment-chart cover and partition of unity globalize this. The positive supports may be larger than the original support, but stay compact in that open. This reconstructs the applied CLD 1.2.6–13 and 6.5.1–3 arguments; their complete statements and immediate proofs were freshly read.

Let T be a middle-positive current, including symmetry as in CLD 7.2.1. For a positive test form η, φ↦〈T,φη〉 is a positive scalar functional. A cutoff plateau bounds it by the supremum norm on compact sets. Density and Riesz extend it to a Radon measure. For β=η_+-η_-, subtract these measures to obtain μ_(T,β). Equality on smooth scalars proves independence of decomposition and support in supp β. Antisymmetric tests pair to zero. Continuous multiplication bT is therefore defined, with
|〈bT,β〉|≤sup_(supp η_+∪supp η_-) |b| ·〈T,η_++η_-〉.

If positive T_j→T weakly and b_j→b locally uniformly, then b_jT_j→bT. For a fixed β choose smooth g uniformly ε-close to b on the compact union of positive supports and split b_jT_j-bT=(b_j-g)T_j+g(T_j-T)+(g-b)T. The bound controls the first and last terms because 〈T_j,η_++η_-〉 stays bounded. The middle term tends to zero; let ε↓0. This proves the needed multiplication continuity. CLD 7.2.8 and 7.2.11–12 provide the scalar/coefficient measure foundations. The printed strong domination in 7.2.9 is not used.

For closed symmetric T and smooth g, Leibniz with complementary test degrees gives d′d″(gT)=d′d″g∧T. For continuous g the left side is defined by order-zero multiplication. Arbitrary continuous multiplication is not asserted to preserve closedness. Smooth local-potential changes with d′d″g=0 leave recursive products unchanged.

On a sheet write f=q+u, g=q+v and define α_u=θ+d′d″[u] and B(u,v)=d′d″(f d′d″[g]). Local smooth-positive approximants give d′d″g_j→d′d″g, and the preceding lemma gives f_j d′d″g_j→f d′d″g. Differentiating proves convergence of their smooth mixed products. These products are symmetric and positive, so the limit is symmetric, positive and independent of both sequences. The smooth-null rule glues it on ordinary overlaps. These are the bounded recursive arguments of CLD 8.5, 8.7 and 8.8; complete applied statements and immediate proofs were read. CLD 15.7.1–2 equips every topologically separated pure n-dimensional analytic space, with its analytic boundary, with its canonical calibrated tropical level n. Applied to our boundaryless surface, the positive top current is an actual analytic Radon measure.

The identity torus moment chart has saturated lattice Z² and analytic degree one. Consequently θ²=2i_*dx, where dx is probability Lebesgue measure on R²/Z². The RAW reference mass is 2; the factor is 2!, not a probability convention. Canonical integration retains its full generic multiplicities. Only smooth identity and translated identity charts, where degree really is one, are used in the explicit calculations. The deeper CLD/Berkovich integration foundations are cited, not claimed to have been rebuilt completely.

Globally B(u,v)=θ∧α_v+d′d″(uα_v) and θ∧α_v=θ²+d′d″(vθ). Pairing differentiated currents with constant 1 on compact boundaryless X gives B(u,v)(X)=2. Put MA_θ(u)=B(u,u). The same argument proves weak continuity under uniform convergence within C_θ. Dini gives decreasing continuity when the decreasing limit is still continuous. No unbounded decreasing-limit assertion follows.

Convex nondecreasing smooth regularizations of max preserve positive Hessians, so max(u,v)∈C_θ. Ordinary locality and equal mass, for w=max(u,v-ε), give
MA_θ(v){u<v-ε}≤2-MA_θ(u){u>v-ε}=MA_θ(u){u≤v-ε}.
Letting ε↓0 gives bounded comparison MA_θ(v){u<v}≤MA_θ(u){u<v}. This is not full-E¹ comparison or uniqueness.

Now construct the branch atom. Let G(y)=y²/2-y/2+1/12 on [0,1], periodically extended, and u_0=-G(x_1)-G(x_2). Its endpoint slope drop gives G″=dy-δ_0. Positive periodic convolutions of -G have 1+h_ε″≥0 and converge uniformly. Their identity-chart diagonal Hessian squares are 2i_*((dy+h_ε″)⊗(dy+h_ε″)), tending to 2δ_(i(0)). The proved operator continuity yields u_0∈C_θ and MA_θ(u_0)=2δ_(i(0)). Its range is [-1/6,1/12].

On V={|x_j|<1/4}, let N≥1, r_N=|t|^N=e^-N, b_j=log max(1,|z_j|), ℓ_(j,N)=log max(r_N,|z_j-1|), d_(j,N)=ℓ_(j,N)-b_j, and D_N=max(d_(1,N),d_(2,N)). Each d_j≤0 and equals zero whenever |z_j|≠1. Hence D_N is nonzero only in the compact fiber F=τ^-1(0)⊂V. Extend it by zero outside V. The extension is continuous, since F lies compactly inside V and the function is zero near every point with at least one |z_j|≠1. Its negative locus is the ordinary open W={|z_j-1|<1 for both j}. Put U_N=u_0+D_N. On V,
q+U_N=max(ℓ_(1,N)+b_2,b_1+ℓ_(2,N))-(1/2)log|z_1z_2|-1/6.
The final log is smooth pluriharmonic. A truncated log is locally constant near its zero, and elsewhere is a convex maximum of invertible-function logarithms. Ordinary moment charts and smooth convex approximations prove U_N∈C_θ, including points z_j-1=0.

Inside W set w_j=z_j-1. The weight is H_N=log max(r_N,|w_1|,|w_2|)-1/6. Let ξ_N be the Gauss point of the closed w-polydisc with both radii r_N. It is an actual point of W. There |z_j-1|=r_N<1, whereas |z_j-1|=1 at i(0), so ξ_N is off the original Gauss section.

Near ξ_N the w_j are invertible and give a translated identity-torus chart with saturated Z² lattice and degree one. Center logarithmic coordinates at r_N. The regularization ε log(1+exp(y_1/ε)+exp(y_2/ε)) of max(0,y_1,y_2) has gradient a diffeomorphism onto the interior of the simplex with vertices 0,e_1,e_2. Change of variables gives Hessian-determinant integral 1/2. Scaling gives concentration at y=0; the CLD exterior square multiplies by 2!, giving mass one. Its smooth measures lie on the translated Gauss section. Continuity of that section gives convergence against analytic continuous tests, and bounded operator continuity identifies the limit. Away from the vertex, the weight is locally affine or, after a pluriharmonic subtraction, depends on one coordinate, so its Hessian square vanishes. At w_j=0 the inactive truncated log can be omitted locally, again giving rank at most one. Therefore
MA_θ(U_N)|W=δ_(ξ_N), and MA_θ(U_N)(X)=2.

The residual mass one outside W is not identified. This proves an analytic atom, not merely its tropical pushforward. Applied primary units include CLD 1.7.7, 5.8.1–6, 8.2.1–3, 12.1.2–5, 14.3.1–5, 14.5.2–3 and 15.7.1–2; complete immediately applied passages were freshly read, with source versions and intervals in source-application-ledger.md. Artifacts are notes/n2.md, P16.7-partial-paper.md and proof-companion.md. The full intrinsic psh and unbounded finite-energy quantifiers remain open.

notes.summary: Exact separable skeletal equations and circle envelopes/energy; all mass-two measures have finite restricted dual energy, which does not imply full admissibility.
notes.detailedSummary: The periodic Green kernel parameterizes dy+h″≥0 circle potentials, proves normalized uniform compactness, and solves every Gauss-section product measure uniquely within S_θ. Explicit energy agrees with the bounded mixed energy, with circle first variation, obstacle envelopes and contact orthogonality. For arbitrary analytic μ the restricted variational maximizer sees only its marginals and returns their skeletal product. At the rigid point (1,1), E*_sep(2δ)=1/6 although the maximizing measure is supported at a different Gauss point.
notes.text:
This is a complete restricted separable, skeletal, bounded equation and envelope theory on (X,θ) of n1–n2, not an intrinsic all-support E¹ theorem. Circle Lebesgue dy has probability mass one; analytic Monge–Ampère measures retain raw mass 2.

Let C=R/Z and H={h∈C(C):ρ_h=dy+h″≥0 distributionally}. Every ρ_h has mass one. The periodic G(y)=y²/2-y/2+1/12 has mean zero and G″=dy-δ_0. For any circle probability ν, h_ν=-G*ν satisfies ρ_(h_ν)=ν. Conversely h-h_(ρ_h) has zero second derivative and is periodic, hence constant. Thus H/R is precisely the circle probabilities. Since G∈[-1/24,1/12] and is 1/2-Lipschitz, mean-zero solutions lie in [-1/12,1/24], are 1/2-Lipschitz and have oscillation ≤1/8. The sup-zero normalized set is uniformly bounded and equicontinuous, hence compact by Arzelà–Ascoli; distributional positivity is closed under uniform limits. This is compactness only in the circle directions.

Put S_θ={h_1∘τ_1+h_2∘τ_2:h_j∈H}. Positive periodic convolution gives smooth uniform approximants with 1+h_j″≥0, so S_θ⊂C_θ. For u=h_1(x_1)+h_2(x_2), v=k_1(x_1)+k_2(x_2), the smooth identity-chart computation and n2's continuity give
B(u,v)=i_*(ρ_(h_1)⊗ρ_(k_2)+ρ_(k_1)⊗ρ_(h_2)),
MA_θ(u)=2i_*(ρ_(h_1)⊗ρ_(h_2)).
Weak convergence of product probabilities follows by density of finite sums of products of circle continuous functions. Continuity of the actual section i gives convergence against analytic continuous tests. These are equalities of measures on X.

Every measure 2i_*(ν_1⊗ν_2) is solved by h_(ν_1)∘τ_1+h_(ν_2)∘τ_2. Marginal recovery and circle uniqueness prove uniqueness modulo constants WITHIN S_θ. No uniqueness against arbitrary C_θ or a larger psh class is asserted.

All h∈H are Lipschitz, and e(h)=∫hdy-(1/2)∫|h′|²dy is finite. Convolution gives uniform convergence of h, L² convergence of derivatives and weak curvature convergence, proving distributional integration by parts ∫h dρ_h=∫hdy-∫|h′|²dy. Consequently
 e(k)-e(h)=∫(k-h)dρ_h-(1/2)∫|k′-h′|²dy.
Thus e is concave, strictly concave modulo constants, with derivative along every admissible circle segment equal to integration against ρ_h.

Define E_sep(u)=2(e(h_1)+e(h_2)). Moving a constant between factors changes neither its value nor the represented u, and E_sep(u+c)=E_sep(u)+2c. Define the bounded mixed energy
E_θ(u)=(1/3)∫_X u(θ²+θ∧α_u+MA_θ(u)).
On S_θ one has θ∧α_u=i_*(ρ_(h_1)⊗dy+dy⊗ρ_(h_2)). Summing the three energy terms makes each factor contribute ∫hdy+∫h dρ_h=2e(h); hence E_θ=E_sep. This checks normalization directly, without claiming energy differentiability in all analytic directions.

For ANY positive analytic Radon μ of mass 2 define E*_sep(μ)=sup_(u∈S_θ)(E_sep(u)-∫u dμ). This lies between 0 and 1/2: normalize both factors by sup h_j=0, giving -1/4≤u≤0 and E_sep(u)≤0; u=0 gives the lower bound. For ν_j=(1/2)(τ_j)_*μ the objective equals 2Σ_j(e(h_j)-∫h_j dν_j). The exact energy-difference identity proves that its maximizing factors, uniquely modulo constants, satisfy ρ_(h_j)=ν_j. Their analytic MA is 2i_*(ν_1⊗ν_2), irrespective of μ's original support or correlation. Finiteness of this restricted dual does not certify full finite energy.

For the K-rational point y=(1,1), μ=2δ_y has both marginals δ_0. Its maximizer is u_0=-G(x_1)-G(x_2). Since ∫|G′|²dy=1/12, E_sep(u_0)=-1/6 and u_0(y)=-1/6, so E*_sep(2δ_y)=1/6. But MA_θ(u_0)=2δ_(i(0)), and i(0)≠y: |z_j-1| is respectively one and zero. This disproves that restricted inverse problem for this restricted-admissible measure; it does not disprove P16.7.

Circle obstacle envelopes have full properties in their exact scope. For continuous a let P(a)=sup{h∈H:h≤a}. Constants make the family nonempty. Its common Lipschitz bound and finite bounds make the supremum finite, continuous and 1/2-Lipschitz. On R, y²/2+P(a)(y) is the supremum of convex functions, hence convex. Thus P(a)∈H and is the largest admissible minorant. Monotonicity and constant translation give ||P(a)-P(b)||_∞≤||a-b||_∞.

Its curvature is supported on {P(a)=a}. If F(y)=y²/2+P(a)(y) had curvature in a noncontact arc, choose a short interval compactly inside that arc, with positive interior curvature and positive obstacle clearance. Replace F on the interval by its endpoint chord. This raises it somewhere, preserves convexity because the chord slope lies between exterior slopes, and stays within clearance when the interval is short, by bounded local slopes. Repeat on integer translates using F(y+n)=F(y)+ny+n²/2. The result gives a larger periodic admissible minorant, contradiction. Therefore ∫(a-P(a))dρ_(P(a))=0.

Let p=P(a), p_b=P(a+bv) for continuous circle v. The difference identity and the two contact-support statements give
b∫v dρ_(p_b)≤e(p_b)-e(p)≤b∫v dρ_p.
Nonexpansiveness gives p_b→p uniformly; distributional testing and fixed mass give ρ_(p_b)→ρ_p weakly. Dividing for either sign of b proves d/db|_0 e(P(a+bv))=∫v dρ_p. Orthogonality and first variation are thereby established in every CIRCLE direction, not for arbitrary analytic obstacles or all analytic directions.

This reconstructs the useful whole373 conclusions through elementary circle analysis and n2's repaired bounded calculus. No imported whole373 result is a premise. Artifacts are notes/n3.md, P16.7-partial-paper.md and proof-companion.md. Own diagnostic checks rerun with `python scripts/diagnostics.py`; they do not establish universal analytic assertions.

notes.summary: New exact branch energy E(U_N)=-1/6-N/3 proves infinite C_θ dual energy of the rigid mass-two atom, despite finite separable dual energy.
notes.detailedSummary: Using ordinary locality and middle coefficient-measure multiplication, D_Nθ=D_Nα_0=0 and the actual off-skeleton atom compute all three mixed energy integrals. The exact values E_θ(U_N)=-1/6-N/3 and U_N(1,1)=-1/6-N give E_θ(U_N)-2U_N(1,1)=1/6+5N/3→∞. Thus the larger bounded dual test excludes this rigid atom. The same conclusion applies to any extension containing these bounded potentials with the same energy; no comparison with an unspecified full psh theory or counterexample to P16.7 is asserted.
notes.text:
The branch potentials U_N of n2 prove that the rigid mass-two atom 2δ_y has infinite dual energy already over C_θ, although its separable dual energy is 1/6 by n3. This is an admissibility result, not a counterexample to the original finite-energy equation.

Use E_θ from n3 and define E*_(C_θ)(μ)=sup_(u∈C_θ)(E_θ(u)-∫u dμ) for μ of mass 2. Each mixed measure has mass 2, so E_θ(u+c)=E_θ(u)+2c and the objective is unchanged by constants. General concavity, compactness or energy differentiation on C_θ is not assumed.

The computation uses ordinary opens and coefficient measures, avoiding an unproved nonsmooth global integration-by-parts identity. Let α_0=θ+d′d″u_0, F=τ^-1(0) and W={|z_1-1|<1,|z_2-1|<1}. On W, x_1=x_2=0, so q and u_0 are constant. Thus θ|W=α_0|W=0. The continuous D_N vanishes outside W, including its boundary. The order-zero coefficient-measure calculus therefore gives D_Nθ=D_Nα_0=0 globally: the currents vanish on W and the multiplier vanishes on its complement.

Since α_(U_N)=α_0+d′d″D_N, smooth-factor multiplication and its continuous extension give θ∧α_(U_N)=θ∧α_0+d′d″(D_Nθ)=θ∧α_0. Outside the closed fiber F, U_N=u_0 on ordinary neighborhoods. Locality and MA_θ(u_0)=2δ_(i(0)) show that MA_θ(U_N) is supported on F. There u_0=-1/6. By n2, MA_θ(U_N)|W=δ_(ξ_N), its total mass is 2 and D_N(ξ_N)=-N. Consequently
∫U_N MA_θ(U_N)=-1/3-N.

D_N is zero everywhere on the original Gauss section: at a unit-radius Gauss point |z_j-1|=1, and elsewhere at least one d_j is zero. Since G has mean zero, ∫U_Nθ²=∫u_0θ²=0. Also θ∧α_0=i_*(dy⊗δ_0+δ_0⊗dy), giving ∫U_N(θ∧α_(U_N))=-1/6. Substitution into the defining three-term energy proves, for EVERY N≥1,
E_θ(U_N)=(0-1/6-1/3-N)/3=-1/6-N/3.

At the actual K-rational point y=(1,1), D_N(y)=-N and u_0(y)=-1/6. Therefore
E_θ(U_N)-2U_N(y)=1/6+5N/3→+∞,
so E*_(C_θ)(2δ_y)=+∞. F_L is not used. Any larger theory containing these bounded locally generated potentials and agreeing with their mixed energy also has infinite dual energy at this atom. Without a class-comparison theorem that is an explicit implication, not identification with an unspecified full psh theory. Dividing both raw measures and energies by 2 preserves divergence.

Since D_N≤0 and u_0 attains its maximum 1/12 outside F, sup U_N=1/12 for every N, while U_N(y)→-∞. This family is not uniformly precompact after sup normalization. Its energies tend to -∞, so it does not disprove compactness on energy-bounded sets or in weaker topologies. The decreasing extended limit is singular at y; no E¹ membership, full mass or unbounded decreasing continuity is claimed.

This proves the precise failure of using restricted finite dual energy as full admissibility. Artifacts are notes/n4.md, P16.7-partial-paper.md, proof-companion.md and evidence/diagnostics.json. `python scripts/diagnostics.py` checks eight rational instances; that finite computation is diagnostic only, while the current-and-measure argument proves the displayed formula for all N.

The mathematical findings are proved in n1–n4. Unconditionally, the specified periods over C((s)) construct a good strict smooth separated proper geometrically connected surface. Its real CLD θ has raw mass 2. Middle-positive coefficient measures give an ordinary-local bounded mixed operator, uniform continuity and bounded comparison. Product measures on its Gauss section are solved uniquely within S_θ; circle compactness, envelopes, orthogonality and first variation hold in those directions. Noninvariant U_N have actual off-canonical-skeleton atoms of mass one. Their energies are -1/6-N/3 and rigid-point values -1/6-N, proving infinite C_θ dual energy of 2δ_(1,1) despite separable dual energy 1/6.

Nonalgebraization is conditional. For any complete extension L/K satisfying Pic(P_m,L)=0 for every finite wide polyannulus in n1, compatible infinite frames trivialize torus line bundles, coefficient recurrence and common pole fractions make every meromorphic function constant, and generic-field/flatness/descent arguments exclude EVERY separated finite-type L-scheme or algebraic-space algebraization. The finite Picard foundation has not been proved or authenticated in sufficient scope. Gruson's pure-product theorem cannot replace arbitrary wide-annulus-base factoriality. Accordingly no unconditional genuine-nonalgebraizability certificate is issued.

Even if that foundation were supplied, the following original completion requirements remain missing:
1. A noncircular FULL intrinsic psh cone and any claimed comparison with the distinct classical curve-test, model PL, ordinary-current, weak-smooth or generated classes.
2. A genuine unbounded E¹/full-mass domain, mixed and top products there, and decreasing continuity beyond continuous bounded limits.
3. Compactness in a specified useful topology and envelope regularity/orthogonality for arbitrary analytic obstacles in ALL analytic directions.
4. Global first variation and the FULL dual-energy condition for analytic measures, with raw mass 2 or a consistent division of both measures and energies by 2.
5. Comparison and uniqueness modulo constants in FULL E¹, and existence for EVERY admissible finite-energy measure with arbitrary analytic support.

No counterexample to the original admissible-measure equation was obtained. The rigid atom tested here is already inadmissible for the larger bounded dual functional. No class-comparison theorem makes it admissible in a full theory. No all-support problem is replaced by a skeletal problem as a purported solution, and no ample line bundle is introduced.
